It's the latest in a series of failures by Meta to keep advertisements for tools that produce nonconsensual intimate imagery off its platforms. The tool, which is called Kromix, bills itself as an "AI image styler." A voice-over for one of the video advertisements, viewed by WIRED, promotes the tool as having "no restrictions," saying "all the characters are real people" and describing it as "the AI that men actually use." In one ad, a woman closely resembling a prominent female US politician is seen in front of a US flag and the flag of the president of the US above the caption "What if she moved?" ai.summary: Nvidia cut its guarantee for OpenAI's Ohio data center to $120B from $250B. The move follows investor concerns, as Anthropic's revenue jump to $11.5B defies bubble fears.

ai.headline: AI books flood Amazon, tanking sales for human authors
ai.summary: AI-generated books make up 20% of Amazon's self-published catalog but bring in only 12% of sales. The findings could provide key data for copyright lawsuits against AI companies.

ai.headline: Amazon Uses Twitch Content to Train AI Unless Streamers Opt Out
ai.summary: Amazon can use Twitch streamers' content to train AI models unless they opt out. Streamers are questioning the ethics of their content being used without explicit permission.

ai.headline: Plaintiff injects invisible AI prompts into filings
ai.summary: A Connecticut plaintiff hid invisible AI instructions in white - on - white court filings to manipulate a review system. The judge revoked the plaintiff's electronic filing privileges, treating it like jury tampering.

ai.headline: World Labs turns one real-world robot task into thousands of simulated variations for training
ai.summary: World Labs, the startup founded by AI pioneer Fei-Fei Li, has unveiled a simulation engine that trains robot controllers entirely in virtual environments. From a single real-world task, the system generates thousands of controlled variations. The trained models then ran for one hour each on five different robot platforms without human intervention.

ai.headline: Study frames AI adoption as tragedy of cognitive commons
ai.summary: Companies cutting entry-level jobs benefit individually, but collective expertise erodes. The loss may surface by 2030 - 2045 when junior talent should have advanced.

ai.headline: Moonshot AI's PerceptionBench reveals GPT-5.6 Sol leads visual perception test
ai.summary: Moonshot AI's PerceptionBench found that no frontier model exceeds 60 percent accuracy on visual perception tasks. The results suggest many reasoning errors stem from early image - reading flaws, highlighting a gap in current multimodal AI.

ai.headline: Anthropic announces watermark detection API that will let third parties detect Claude's AI texts
ai.summary: Anthropic will soon offer a watermark detection API that lets third parties check whether text was written by Claude. The technology builds on Google's SynthID method and tweaks the randomness during word selection without affecting text quality, Anthropic says. The approach has limits with fact-heavy text, code, and heavy rewriting.

ai.headline: China's Unitree G1 Robot Goes Viral Online
ai.summary: The 4-foot-tall robot has gained fame as an affordable option that can engage audiences. Its viral success raises questions about whether it can transition from novelty to practical workplace use.

ai.headline: Man Injected AI Prompts in Court Filings to Win Case
ai.summary: A Connecticut judge identified hidden AI-readable text in court documents, the first known instance of a plaintiff attempting to use AI to influence a legal ruling. The tactic raises questions about AI's role in judicial processes and potential future legal strategies involving machine-readable evidence.

ai.headline: Qwen 3.8 Models Go Open Weights With Apache 2.0 License
ai.summary: Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen 3.8 models with open weights under the Apache 2.0 license. The dense 27-billion-parameter model targets local and agent-based applications with improved coding and office task performance.

ai.headline: OpenAI Records Mac Clicks Into Searchable ChatGPT Timeline
ai.summary: OpenAI's Computer History records clicks, keystrokes, and app switches on Mac and creates a searchable timeline for ChatGPT and Codex. The system stores this data locally as unencrypted Markdown files, though OpenAI states it isn't used for training while memories could still reach training data.

harvest.summary: Businesses are willing to flop back and forth as each lab releases new models, volatility that should give both companies' investors pause about how "sticky" enterprise AI spending really is.

harvest.headline: Google Discover is getting an AI chatbot-tuned feed
harvest.summary: Google will soon allow you to customize your Discover feed by describing what you want to see. The new feature , rolling out to the Google app in the "coming days," will use AI to automatically tweak your feed and "remember" your preferences for future visits. You'll find the option within the three-dot menu on your Discover feed.

harvest.headline: Adobe Firefly adds AI audio tools and Google's Gemini Omni Flash
harvest.summary: Adobe is making three AI audio tools broadly available in Firefly. Generate Music, Generate Speech, and Generate Sound Effects create royalty-free music, voiceovers, and sound effects for video projects. Adobe has also added Gemini Omni Flash to the platform.

harvest.headline: Paving the way for greener ammonia production
harvest.summary: Ammonia is one of the most important chemicals produced in the world, ranking second only to sulfuric acid in the total volume produced each year. It is used mostly to make fertilizer, which is essential to feeding the world's population. Yet its production accounts for up to 2 percent of the world's energy consumption and about 1.5 percent of greenhouse gas emissions, so the search has been underway for ways to produce ammonia more sustainably.

harvest.headline: Grok exfiltrates user data when malicious instructions are encrypted
harvest.summary: Earlier this week, researchers outlined an attack that used a secret input provided by Microsoft 365 Copilot for enterprise to cause the AI assistant to exfiltrate a password present in the user's inbox. Now, a separate team has devised a similar attack against Grok. The new data theft hack employs a deceptively simple trick to force the Elon Musk-owned large language model to steal user chats and other personal information.

harvest.headline: Meta ran ads for an app promising to nudify female politicians
harvest.summary: Meta platforms recently ran ads for an AI porn-generation tool that seemingly encouraged users to create deepfaked videos resembling female US politicians, despite the company's policies against ads containing sexual material. It's the latest in a series of failures by Meta to keep advertisements for tools that produce nonconsensual intimate imagery off its platforms. The tool, which is called Kromix, bills itself as an "AI image styler." A voice-over for one of the video advertisements, viewed by WIRED, promotes the tool as having "no restrictions," saying "all the characters are real people" and describing it as "the AI that men actually use." In one ad, a woman closely resembling a prominent female US politician is seen in front of a US flag and the flag of the president of the US above the caption "What if she moved?" She then winks, before the ad cuts to a scene of a woman with the same face performing in a pornographic video.

harvest.headline: Flock is tightening its rules in response to a growing surveillance backlash
harvest.summary: Tightening the rules: Flock, whose cameras form a nationwide police surveillance network, is now requiring officers to enter a criminal case number before searching location data - a basic safeguard civil liberties groups have long demanded. Easy to game: Since Flock won't verify case numbers, officers could bypass the new rule just as easily as previous ones - like when some entered "hehehe" 20 times in response to a prompt asking why they were conducting a search. A backlash from all sides: At least 30 cities dropped Flock contracts in the past year, with critics ranging from the ACLU to Tucker Carlson, while some states are moving to ban license plate readers altogether.

harvest.headline: How kids feel about AI, in their own words
harvest.summary: When we set out to talk to kids about artificial intelligence, we thought we knew what we'd hear. We expected some to tell us they were using it to cheat a little, the way Millennials and Gen Xers opened up CliffsNotes or programmed formulas into their TI-82s, and others to share inspiring ways they were using it. We were also listening for concerns that were less kid-specific, like deepfakes or job destruction.

harvest.headline: With a feel for physics, AI models simulate a wider range of real-world scenarios
harvest.summary: Artificial intelligence models are jacks of many trades, including writing, generating images, and creating 3D models. But they aren't as helpful when it comes to testing robots or designs for vehicles in diverse environments, since they don't understand physics as well as they do pixels or text. To build an AI system that can reliably simulate a variety of physical scenarios, engineers need a range of physics data at a scale that isn't yet feasible.

harvest.headline: Alexander Rakhlin named director of the MIT Statistics and Data Science Center
harvest.summary: Alexander "Sasha" Rakhlin PhD '06, the Distinguished Professor in Data, Systems, and Society at the MIT Institute for Data, Systems, and Society (IDSS); a professor of brain and cognitive sciences at MIT; and a principal investigator in the MIT Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems (LIDS) has been named the next director of the MIT Statistics and Data Science Center (SDSC). Rakhlin succeeds Ankur Moitra, the Norbert Wiener Professor of Mathematics, associate director of the IDSS, and a faculty member in the MIT Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) who has been SDSC director since 2021. Philippe Rigollet, the Cecil and Ida Green Distinguished Professor of Mathematics and a core faculty member in IDSS, also served as interim director in 2024-25.

harvest.headline: Gemini Robotics ER 2: powering robotics with video understanding, task orchestration, and multi-robot collaboration
harvest.summary: Gemini Robotics ER 2 helps robots reason, collaborate, and solve real-world tasks. It represents a step change in video understanding, tool orchestration, and multi-robot collaboration for robotic applications.

harvest.headline: Google just redesigned the search box for the first time in 25 years - here's why it matters more than you think.
harvest.summary: For a quarter century, the Google search box has been one of the most recognizable interfaces in computing: a thin white rectangle, a blinking cursor, a few typed words, and a list of blue links. On Tuesday, Google will formally retire that paradigm. At its annual I/O developer conference , Google announced a sweeping redesign of the search box itself - the literal text field where billions of queries begin every day - transforming it from a simple keyword input into a dynamic, AI-driven conversation starter that can accept text, images, PDFs, videos, and even open Chrome tabs as inputs.
